topic: Steve Yegge’s perspective on AI agents reshaping software engineering practices
sourceTitle: Steve Yegge on AI Agents and the Future of Software Engineering
postText:
AI agents are rewriting the rulebook for software engineering.

- I listened to Steve Yegge’s recent talk and one thing stuck: AI can now draft, refactor, and even design code snippets without human prompts.
It can spin up a micro-service skeleton in seconds, something that used to take hours.

- But Yegge warns that relying on AI for the “creative” parts can erode our deep problem-solving muscles, especially when the models hallucinate architectural constraints.
Yegge also notes that this over-reliance can blind teams to hidden performance bottlenecks.

- In practice, I’ve started using an LLM to generate boilerplate, then spend 20-30% of the sprint reviewing its output. The time saved on repetitive tasks is real, yet the review cost balances it out.
In my last sprint, the AI-generated scaffolding shaved off 8 hours of manual wiring, freeing time for user-focused testing.

- The real opportunity, according to Yegge, is using agents as “pair programmers” that surface alternatives we’d never think of, forcing us to question our own assumptions.
That frictionless ideation has already helped my team discover a caching pattern that cut latency by 30% in a side project.

- However, we must embed guardrails: unit-test coverage, static analysis, and a clear ownership model so the AI never becomes a black box.
A simple policy-no production merge without passing the full test suite-has kept us from accidental regressions.

How are you blending AI agents into your development workflow without losing the craft?
